Malaysia has 20 public universities, including globally ranked institutions such as Universiti Malaya, Universiti Sains Malaysia, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Universiti Putra Malaysia and Universiti Teknologi Malaysia. For international students, that makes Malaysia one of Asia’s most practical study destinations.

You get recognised degrees, English-taught programmes, multicultural student life and a cost of living that is often lower than the UK, USA, Canada and Australia.

The short answer is this: public universities in Malaysia are government-funded higher education institutions, also known as government universities in Malaysia or Universiti Awam. They are part of Malaysia’s national higher education system and include several strong research universities.

How Many Public Universities Are There in Malaysia?

Malaysia has 20 public universities. The official Ministry of Higher Education public university directory lists these institutions under Malaysia’s public higher education system.

The top public universities in Malaysia include Universiti Malaya, Universiti Sains Malaysia, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Universiti Putra Malaysia and Universiti Teknologi Malaysia.

According to the QS World University Rankings 2027 for Malaysia, Universiti Malaya ranks 56th globally, followed by Universiti Sains Malaysia at =128, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia at 130, Universiti Putra Malaysia at 138 and Universiti Teknologi Malaysia at =158.

If you are still comparing countries, start with your wider overseas study plan before choosing Malaysia.

Detailed Overview of the Top 10 Public Universities in Malaysia

Here are the top 10 public universities in Malaysia with practical overviews. This section focuses on what students actually need: ranking strength, subject areas, estimated tuition fees, duration, location and the real reason each university may suit a particular student.

1. Universiti Malaya (UM)

Universiti Malaya is widely regarded as the best public university in Malaysia. Located in Kuala Lumpur, UM gives students the strongest mix of global reputation, research strength and capital-city access. It suits students who want a degree with strong recognition across Asia and beyond.

UM ranks 56th in the QS World University Rankings 2027, making it the highest-ranked Malaysian university. It is a strong choice for medicine, law, business, engineering, arts and social sciences.

The main trade-off is cost. Kuala Lumpur can be more expensive than smaller Malaysian cities, and high-demand programmes may carry higher fees. Still, for students who want reputation, networking and city exposure, UM is usually the first public university to compare.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Medicine, law, business, engineering, humanities
  • Why choose it: Strongest overall reputation and capital-city access
  • Fee note: Programme-based; medicine and clinical subjects can be significantly higher
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–4 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Kuala Lumpur
  • Official source to check: current UM programmes and fees

2. Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM)

Universiti Sains Malaysia is one of Malaysia’s strongest research universities and a smart option for science-focused students. Its main campus is in Penang, a city many students find easier to live in than Kuala Lumpur while still enjoying a strong academic and cultural environment.

USM ranks =128 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. It is especially strong for science, medicine, pharmacy, health sciences and sustainability-related fields.

A student choosing USM is often choosing depth over glamour. It may not offer the same capital-city feel as UM, but it gives serious science and research students a strong public university route with a more balanced lifestyle.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Science, medicine, pharmacy, health sciences, sustainability
  • Why choose it: Strong research identity with a Penang cost and lifestyle advantage
  • Fee note: Science and health-related programmes vary widely; clinical subjects cost more
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–5 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Penang
  • Official source to check: current USM programmes and fees

3. Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM)

Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia is a leading public research university in Selangor. It is a strong option for students who want medicine, law, education, health sciences or social sciences. UKM also has a national research role, which adds weight for students looking at postgraduate study.

UKM ranks 130 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. Its location in Bangi gives students access to the wider Kuala Lumpur area without placing them directly in the busiest part of the capital.

UKM is often a good middle-ground choice: strong ranking, strong subjects and a location that can feel calmer than central Kuala Lumpur.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Medicine, law, education, health sciences, social sciences
  • Why choose it: Strong public research profile with access to the capital region
  • Fee note: Programme-based; medical, science and laboratory-based courses can cost more
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–5 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Bangi, Selangor
  • Official source to check: current UKM programmes and fees

4. Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM)

Universiti Putra Malaysia started with a strong agricultural focus, but today it offers a wide range of programmes across science, engineering, business, medicine, bioscience and veterinary fields. It is located in Serdang, close enough to Kuala Lumpur for access while still offering a campus-based study environment.

UPM ranks 138 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. It is one of the best public universities in Malaysia for agriculture, bioscience and veterinary-related subjects.

UPM is a strong choice for students who want a science-led university without choosing a purely technology-focused institution. For agriculture, food science, bioscience and veterinary interests, it deserves serious attention.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Agriculture, bioscience, veterinary science, engineering, business
  • Why choose it: Excellent for bioscience, food, agriculture and veterinary-related routes
  • Fee note: Agriculture and business may be more manageable than clinical programmes
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–4 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Serdang, Selangor
  • Official source to check: current UPM programmes and fees

5. Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM)

Universiti Teknologi Malaysia is one of the strongest government universities in Malaysia for engineering, architecture and technology. Students who want civil engineering, mechanical engineering, computing, built environment or technology-related programmes should keep UTM high on their shortlist.

UTM ranks =158 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. Its main campus is in Johor, which can be practical for students who want a strong technical university outside Kuala Lumpur.

Here is the important point: UTM may be more valuable for an engineering student than some universities that rank higher overall. Subject fit matters more than the headline rank.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Engineering, architecture, computing, technology
  • Why choose it: One of Malaysia’s strongest technical and engineering-focused public universities
  • Fee note: Engineering and technology programmes usually sit above arts and social science fees
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 4 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Johor Bahru, Johor
  • Official source to check: current UTM programmes and fees

6. Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM)

Universiti Utara Malaysia is known for business, management, accounting, economics and public administration. It is located in Kedah, away from the higher living costs of Kuala Lumpur. That makes it attractive for students who want a more budget-conscious study environment.

UUM ranks =540 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. It may not be in the top five overall, but for business and management-focused students, it can be a very sensible public university choice.

This is where ranking alone can mislead students. A business student with a fixed budget may find UUM more practical than a higher-ranked university in a more expensive city.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Business, management, accounting, economics, public administration
  • Why choose it: Strong management focus with lower living-cost potential
  • Fee note: Often more budget-friendly overall because of location and subject mix
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–4 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Sintok, Kedah
  • Official source to check: current UUM programmes and fees

7. Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM)

Universiti Teknologi MARA is one of Malaysia’s largest public higher education institutions. It offers a wide range of programmes in business, law, design, applied sciences, hospitality, communication and technology. Its main campus is in Shah Alam, with many campuses across Malaysia.

UiTM ranks =549 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. It is a useful option for students looking for broad subject coverage and practical, career-focused programmes.

UiTM is not only about ranking. Its real strength is scale, subject variety and practical education. Students who want applied courses, design, business or professional fields should compare its relevant faculties carefully.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Business, law, design, applied sciences, hospitality
  • Why choose it: Broad subject coverage and practical programme options
  • Fee note: Programme-based and may vary by campus, course and level
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–4 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Shah Alam, Selangor
  • Official source to check: current UiTM programmes and fees

8. Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA)

Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah is a strong public university for engineering, technology and applied science. It is a good option for students who want technical programmes with a practical industry focus.

UMPSA ranks =588 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. Because it is outside Kuala Lumpur, some students may find the total living cost more manageable than studying in the capital area.

UMPSA is especially worth considering if you want engineering but also want to manage your budget carefully. It may not have the same name recognition as UM or UTM, but for applied technical study, it can be a strong fit.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Engineering, technology, applied science, computing
  • Why choose it: Practical technical focus with a potentially lower living-cost base
  • Fee note: Engineering and technical programmes often cost more than classroom-based subjects
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 4 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Pahang
  • Official source to check: current UMPSA programmes and fees

9. International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM)

International Islamic University Malaysia is a public university known for combining academic study with Islamic values. It attracts students from many Muslim-majority countries and offers programmes in law, Islamic studies, medicine, engineering, economics, architecture and social sciences.

IIUM ranks =691 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. It is especially relevant for students who want a multicultural campus with strong Islamic studies, law and professional programmes.

For Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Middle Eastern and Muslim international students, IIUM can feel culturally familiar while still offering a serious academic environment.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Islamic studies, law, medicine, engineering, economics
  • Why choose it: Strong Islamic academic environment with international student appeal
  • Fee note: Medicine and clinical subjects cost more; humanities and Islamic studies may be lower
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–5 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Gombak, Selangor
  • Official source to check: current IIUM programmes and fees

10. Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT)

Universiti Malaysia Terengganu is a public university with strong links to marine science, fisheries, ocean studies and environmental subjects. It is a smart choice for students who want a more specialised university rather than a general city-based institution.

UMT ranks 701–710 in the QS World University Rankings 2027. It may not be the highest-ranked university overall, but for marine-related subjects, it deserves attention.

This is a good example of why students should not judge by overall rank only. If your subject is marine science or fisheries, UMT may be more relevant than a higher-ranked university that does not focus on your field.

Key facts:

  • Best for: Marine science, fisheries, ocean studies, environmental studies
  • Why choose it: Strong fit for marine and coastal study routes
  • Fee note: Often more affordable overall than many capital-city options, depending on course
  • Undergraduate duration: Usually 3–4 years
  • Postgraduate duration: Usually 1–3 years
  • Location: Kuala Nerus, Terengganu
  • Official source to check: current UMT programmes and fees

Public Universities in Malaysia for International Students

Public universities in Malaysia attract international students because they offer recognised degrees, English-taught programmes and relatively affordable tuition fees. Students from Bangladesh, Pakistan, India, Nigeria, the Middle East and other regions often choose Malaysia because it feels accessible, culturally familiar and financially more manageable than many Western countries.

Small document mistakes can delay an application. For example, a missing English certificate or unclear passport scan can slow down the Student Pass process. Students applying from Bangladesh can prepare documents before applying instead of waiting until the offer stage.

Tuition Fees at Public Universities in Malaysia

Tuition fees depend on the university, programme and level of study. As a safe planning range, many international undergraduate students can expect public university tuition fees in Malaysia to fall around RM 11,000 to RM 25,000 per year. Science, engineering, computing and clinical subjects may cost more. Medicine, dentistry and pharmacy can be much higher.

Cheapest Public Universities in Malaysia

The cheapest public university in Malaysia depends on your course, study level and lifestyle. Still, students who want a lower total cost should look beyond Kuala Lumpur.

Public universities in Kedah, Perlis, Terengganu, Kelantan and Perak may offer a more affordable student life because rent, food and transport can be lower than in the capital area.

Here is the counterintuitive part: the “cheapest” university on paper may not be the cheapest for your full degree. A slightly higher tuition fee in a city with better part-time access, cheaper accommodation or stronger course outcomes may still be the smarter choice.

Cost of Living in Malaysia

Malaysia is usually more affordable than the UK, USA, Canada and Australia. Many students can plan around RM 1,000 to RM 2,500 per month for living costs, depending on location and lifestyle.

Kuala Lumpur gives students better access to events, internships and networking. But Penang, Kedah, Perlis, Terengganu, Kelantan, Sabah and Sarawak may offer a quieter and cheaper student life. That is not a small detail. Over three or four years, monthly cost differences can become a serious amount.

For families comparing several destinations, Malaysia should also be reviewed alongside other affordable study abroad choices.

Admission Process for Public Universities in Malaysia

The admission process is not complicated, but you need to follow the right order.

Start with the course, not the university name. A famous university may not always be the best fit for your subject, budget or entry profile. Once you choose your subject, shortlist five to seven public universities and compare requirements.

A typical application process looks like this:

  1. Choose your course and university.
  2. Check academic and English language requirements.
  3. Prepare transcripts, certificates, passport and supporting documents.
  4. Submit the university application online.
  5. Wait for the offer letter.
  6. Apply for Student Pass after receiving the offer.
  7. Pay fees and enrol.

Students who need help with course selection, documents and application timing can speak with an adviser before choosing a university.

Scholarships for Public Universities in Malaysia

Common scholarship routes include Malaysia International Scholarship, university merit scholarships, faculty or department awards, postgraduate research assistantships and external scholarships from home-country organisations.

Malaysia may not always offer the largest scholarship packages, but it often gives students a strong balance of lower tuition, shorter travel distance from South Asia and recognised English-medium education. Bangladeshi students can also compare Malaysia with wider fully funded scholarship routes.

Public Universities in Malaysia for Bangladeshi Students

Malaysia is practical for many Bangladeshi students. It is closer than the UK or Canada, halal food is easy to find, the climate feels familiar, and the total cost can be manageable with the right course and city.

Approximate annual study and living cost can range from RM 30,000 to RM 60,000+, depending on course, city and lifestyle. Medical and clinical programmes can go higher.

If Malaysia is one of several destinations on your list, compare it with your wider route from Bangladesh to overseas study before making a final decision.

How to Choose the Right Public University in Malaysia

Do not choose only by ranking. Choose by fit.

A simple shortlist method works well:

  1. Pick your subject.
  2. Choose five to seven public universities.
  3. Remove universities that are outside your budget.
  4. Check entry requirements.
  5. Compare city living costs.
  6. Review scholarship chances.
  7. Apply early.

FAQs About Public Universities in Malaysia

How many public universities are in Malaysia?

Malaysia has 20 public universities. These are government-funded institutions under Malaysia’s higher education system and are also known as Universiti Awam.

What are the top 10 public universities in Malaysia?

The top 10 public universities in Malaysia include UM, USM, UKM, UPM, UTM, UUM, UiTM, UMPSA, IIUM and UMT.

What is the best public university in Malaysia?

Universiti Malaya is widely considered the best public university in Malaysia. It is the highest-ranked Malaysian university in the QS World University Rankings 2027.

Is Universiti Malaya public or private?

Universiti Malaya is a public university. It is based in Kuala Lumpur and is Malaysia’s highest-ranked public university.

What is the tuition fee for public universities in Malaysia?

Many international students should budget around RM 11,000 to RM 25,000 per year for undergraduate tuition. Science, engineering and medical courses can cost more.

What is the cheapest public university in Malaysia?

There is no single cheapest option for every student. UUM, UniMAP, UMT, UMK and UPSI may offer lower living-cost advantages because of their locations.

What is the difference between public and private universities in Malaysia?

Public universities are usually government-funded and often more affordable. Private universities may offer flexible intakes, modern facilities and industry-linked courses, but fees can be higher.

Are public universities in Malaysia good for international students?

Yes. Many public universities in Malaysia accept international students and offer English-taught programmes at relatively affordable fees.

Do Malaysian public universities require IELTS?

Some do, but requirements vary by university and course. Many accept IELTS, TOEFL or other approved English proof. Some students may qualify through previous English-medium study.

Can Bangladeshi students apply to public universities in Malaysia?

Which government university in Malaysia is best for engineering?

Universiti Teknologi Malaysia is one of the strongest government universities in Malaysia for engineering. UMPSA, UM and UPM are also good options depending on the engineering field.

Which public university is best for business in Malaysia?

Universiti Utara Malaysia is well known for business, management and economics. UM, UKM and UiTM are also popular choices.

Is a government university in Malaysia better than a private university?

Not always. Public universities are often more affordable and research-focused, while private universities may offer flexible intakes and stronger industry links in some fields.

Is a top 10 public university in Malaysia list enough to choose from?

Final Advice

If you want a safe shortlist, start with UM, USM, UKM, UPM and UTM. If budget matters more, also compare UUM, UniMAP, UMT, UPSI, UMK and UMPSA. Malaysia has enough public university options for different goals. The key is matching the university with your subject, budget and future plan.

Students who want guided support can speak with an adviser before choosing a university.
